Commentary.Commentary: The second innings is set to begin. Pakistan players make their way out on the field. Followed by the opening pair of New Zealand, Finn Allen and Devon Conway. It will be Mohammad Hasnain to start with the new ball. Here we go...
... The Run Chase ...

New Zealand were right on top from the word go. Lockie Ferguson drew first blood in his very first over. Soon, Michael Bracewell came into the attack inside the first Powerplay and got rid of Babar Azam to put the hosts in a spot of bother. Later, the Kiwis found it really difficult in the middle as nothing was going their way. But once, the third-wicket stand was broken, New Zealand got a sniff and made the most of it. Henry Nicholls had a huge impact in the field as a substitute fielder with his two run outs. Tim Southee stood out with the ball with his three-fer. The onus now is on the New Zealand batters. They need to start on a positive note and not lost early wickets. The series in on the line here. An enticing chase coming your way shortly. Who will get over the line? Do join us shortly for the second essay.

Pakistan were put right under the pump early on, when Shan Masood and Babar Azam were sent back to the dressing room inside Powerplay 1. Later, Mohammad Rizwan and Fakhar Zaman took the matter into their own hands and accelerated their innings really well. Both of them took their time at the crease before shifting the gears. The two stitched a solid stand of 154 runs which stood out and put Pakistan right back on track. Fakhar Zaman went on to make his 100 but Rizwan was unable to covert his score into a three-digit one. Although, both the set batters were sent back in a jiffy. The lower-middle order hit a few lusty blows and took the score to 280.

New Zealand would be a bit disappointed with the way they leaked runs in the final five overs - 49 runs in total. At one stage, it looked like Pakistan could easily get over the 300-run mark here but the Kiwis did really well to pull things back. Nonetheless, Pakistan have got an above par score here and would think their bowlers have enough to defend here.
FOUR! On a length and on off, Mohammad Hasnain moves across and smokes it over mid off for a boundary. Pakistan ends their innings for 280/9.
On a length and outside off, slower too. Mohammad Hasnain looks to slap it but misses.
Mohammad Hasnain is the last man in.

OUT! TAKEN! Fuller and on off, Mohammad Wasim hangs back and looks to loft it but gets the toe end of his bat. It goes high up in the air towards mid off. Kane Williamson settles under it and pouches it comfortably.
Commentary.Howout: c Kane Williamson b Lockie Ferguson

Commentary.Commentary: Lockie Ferguson goes for the yorker but it comes out as a low full toss, wide outside off. Mohammad Wasim slashes, it runs down to third man off the outer half. They take two as the fielder does well in the deep to save a boundary.
Back of a length, outside off. Wasim pulls it over mid-wicket and gets a couple.
A dot now! A slower short ball, outside off. Wasim looks to chase it but misses.
On a length and on off, Mohammad Wasim turns it to mid-wicket for one.
Fuller and on off, Haris Rauf drills it to long off for one.

OUT! TAKEN! Agha Salman's cameo comes to an end. A slower ball into the pitch, Salman looks to sweep it away uppishly straight towards Doug Bracewell (sub) who takes a comfortable catch. Haris Rauf is the next batter on the crease.
Commentary.Howout: c sub Doug Bracewell b Tim Southee

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR MORE! Length ball here, Salman moves across and plays the ramp shot over keeper's head for another boundary!
FOUR! Fine shot. Fuller nad on off, Agha Salman drives it through deep covers for a boundary!

Fuller and on off, Mohammad Wasim pulls it away to the short mid-wicket fielder for a quick run. The fielder has a shy at the bowlers end but misses. A direct hit would have sent him back into the hut.

On a length and outside off, Agha Salman looks to play at it but misses.

A loud roar from the crown as Fakhar Zaman scampers across for a single and reaches his ton. His eighth in the ODIs. It is flatter and on off stump. Zaman opens the face late and guides it towards point for a single.

Drinks break! Pakistan have risen from the ashes here. They lost two early wickets and it the Kiwis certainly had them by the scruff of the neck, although they could not capitalize on it. Mohammad Rizwan and Fakhar Zaman have stitched a solid stand of more than 150 runs to stable the ship for the hosts. Both the batters would be eyeing their respective tons here before going all-out in the death overs. New Zealand need a wicket or two to get back in this contest.

Tim Southee sees the batter charge down the wicket and serves it short, angled down leg. Fakhar Zaman pulls it behind square on the leg side quite awkwardly and takes a single.

This is similar to the last delivery, Fakhar Zaman defends it back again.
Full and around off, Fakhar Zaman defends it back to the bowler.
On off again, some turn to offer, Fakhar Zaman prods forward and defends it.
Bowls it on off, this is defended back.
Fuller length, around off, Rizwan drills it down to long on for a single.
Fuller and on middle, this is defended back towards the bowler.
Powerplay 1 comes to an end! Now, four fielders can be placed outside the inner circle until the end of the 40th over.
Full and on off, defended out to covers. 8 runs off the over. Positive for the hosts.
FOUR! Good shot! It is a short ball, outside off. Zaman rocks back and punches it through the gap at covers. The outfield is quick and the two fielders giving it a chase here have no chance.
Full and on leg, clipped to mid-wicket.
Woah! Close! It is flatter, outside off, it holds its line. Zaman hangs his blade away from his body and gets beaten on the outside edge.
FOUR! Fakhar Zaman riding on his luck here. It is tossed up, on off. Zaman gets a thick outside edge but it flies past the keeper and runs down to the third man fence.
On off, defended to point.

Catch is the call but it lands safely. It is tossed up, full and on off. Zaman gets low and goes for the sweep. The ball takes the top-edge and goes towards deep square leg. It falls in no man's land. One taken.
Michael Bracewell goes full once again, attacking the stumps. Zaman flicks it towards mid on but it results in yet another dot.
Fakhar Zaman defends this full ball off his front foot.
Around off, pushed to covers.
Full and on off, worked to mid-wicket off the inside edge.
Michael Bracewell goes full, wide outside off. Zaman drives it to point.
Mitchell Santner goes full, on middle and leg. Rizwan strides forward and defends it to the leg side.
Another single this time. Fuller and on off, turning into the batter, Zaman nudges it to the leg side and crosses.
This is full, on leg. Rizwan sweeps it to deep square leg. There is protection in the deep. They only get a single.
Short, outside off, turning away. Rizwan leaves it alone.

FOUR! First boundary for Rizwan. It is full, spilled down leg. Mohammad Rizwan gets down on one knee and sweeps it down to fine leg. It races away to the fence. Mohammad Rizwan is making his inent clear.
It is full, outside off, angled in. Mohammad Rizwan defends it to the off side off the front foot.
A wicket-taking over by Michael Bracewell comes to an end. It is full and on off. Zaman pushes it to the off side. Pakistan in a spot of bother here. Mohammad Rizwan has a lot of work to do here.
Full and outside off, blocked out.
Bracewell loops it full and outside off. Rizwan gets forward and knocks it down to long on for a single.
Mohammad Rizwan comes in at number 4.

OUT! STUMPED! Michael Bracewell gets the breakthrough on just his third delivery here. There is a pin-drop silence across the stadium here as the Pakistan skipper departs. Michael Bracewell tosses it up, around off, it turns away a touch. Babar Azam comes down the track and tries to defend it into the deck but gets beaten by the turn here. Tom Latham gathers the ball and takes the bails off in a flash. Babar Azam is clearly out of the crease and the square leg umpire raises his finger. No need to go to the third umpire this time. New Zealand right on top here.
Commentary.Howout: st Tom Latham b Michael Bracewell

Commentary.Commentary: This one is sliding down leg. Zaman clips it through square leg for a single.
It is a short ball, outside off. Zaman stands back and cuts it through point. They take a couple.
Change. More spin now as Michael Bracewell replaces Tim Southee.
Babar Azam charges down the wicket and flicks this full delivery from outside off to mid-wicket. The fielder there makes a great diving stop. No runs this time.
On off, defended.
FOUR! Babar Azam tickles it fine and gets off the mark with a boundary. It is too straight, sliding down leg. Azam hangs back and glances it around the corner.
Mitchell Santner comes 'round the wicket for Azam. It is a length ball, on middle, coming in with the arm. Azam stays back and nudges it to mid-wicket.
A single now as Zaman clips it full delivery through mid-wicket.
Loops it up, just outside off. Zaman opens the face and blocks it out.
Change. Time for some early spin now, as Mitchell Santner comes into the attack.
Goes full this time once again, just outside off. Azam dabs it towards point, but not in the gap. Pakistan under the pump here.
Full and on off, defended back to the bowler.
It is full, angling across the left-hander. Zaman leans it and tries to drive it towards extra cover but catches the outside edge. It goes to backward point for one.

FOUR! Gets fortunate this time. It is a short ball, on the bodyline. Fakhar Zaman tries to heave it across the line. The ball flies towards fine leg off the top edge. A couple of bounces into the ropes.
Much fuller, just outside off. Zaman presses forward and defends it back to the bowler. Two dots!
Back of a length, angled across the left-hander. Fakhar Zaman watches it sail past him.
Two dots in a row to end the over. Fraction short, on fourth stump. Azam uses the depth of his crease and clips it to the leg side.
It is fuller, just outside off. Azam strides and nudges it in front of mid on.
Ferguson dishes a length ball this time, on off. Zaman inside-edges it to square leg. The batters cross for one.
Full length, outside off. Zaman closes the face and flicks it to mid-wicket.

FOUR! Easy pickings! First boundary of the innings for the hosts. Lockie Ferguson goes full, straying on the pads. Zaman clips it through the mid-wicket region off his pads. It races away and the fans have something to cheer for here.
A short ball, angling across. Zaman keeps his bat to himself.

Full length, swinging away a touch, on fifth stump. Azam gets forward and taps it back to the bowler. Tim Southee collects it on a bounce and dummies a throw at the striker's end. Just a single off the over. Tim Southee has conceded just 2 runs off his two overs so far.
Make that three! Babar Azam is yet to get off the mark. Fraction short, in the channel. It gets some extra bounce off the deck. Azam stands tall and jabs it to cover-point.
Two dots now on the trot! On a length, around off. Azam knocks it back to the bowler off his front foot.
So, there is a slip in place for Azam now. Southee goes full, on fifth stump. Azam gets behinds and defends it out solidly.
Good length, around off. Zaman taps it to mid off and crosses for a single.
Tim Southee goes full, wide outside off. This one does not bounce much off the deck. Zaman lets it be.
Babar Azam is the new man in.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! It is a length ball, that lands on leg and angles across the left-hander. Shan Masood tries to block it but misses. The ball zips past the outside edge. There is an appeal for caught behind but the umpire shows no interest. Kane Williamson thinks about it and takes the review. The UltraEdge later confirms that there is spike as the ball passes the bat. The big screen shows OUT and Pakistan lose an early wicket. Shan Masood is unable to have a solid impact on his return and trudges back on a 2-ball duck.
Commentary.Howout: c Tom Latham b Lockie Ferguson

Commentary.Commentary: Shan Masood presses forward to this full ball and defends it to mid off.
Lockie Ferguson fires a full-length ball, on leg stump. Fakhar Zaman hangs back and clips it through square leg off his pads for a single.
Length and on off, defended out watchfully.

Lockie Ferguson steams in and serves a length ball, around off, angling across the left-hander. It gets some good bounce and carry as well. Fakhar Zaman stays inside his crease and tries to have a poke at it. Gets beaten on the outside edge this time.
Good length, wide of off. Zaman is happy with a sighter here and leaves it alone.

No, he cannot! Southee now offer some width to the batter, on a length. Zaman stays back and slashes it through the vacant backward point region for a single. A solid start for the visitors. Lockie Ferguson to bowl from the other end.
Southee fires it full and on off. Zaman drives it down to mid off, but straight at the fielder. WIll Southee start his spell with a maiden here?
A length ball, on fifth stump. Zaman hangs back and knocks it towards point. Pakistan are yet to get off the mark here.
Goes full again, around middle. Zaman gets forward and eases it to mid on.
It is full, attacking the leg stump. Zaman stays back and nudges it to mid-wicket.
A stifled appeal for lbw! Tim Southee gets the ball to talk early on. It is a length ball, angled across, it lands on off and nips back in. Fakhar Zaman gets an inside edge on his pads.
We are all set for the game to begin. The umpires and the players are out in the middle. Fakhar Zaman and Shan Masood are the openers for Pakistan. Tim Southee to start with the ball. Here we go...

Pitch Report - Danny Morrison and Waqar Younis are near the deck. The teams are going to play on a new surface. Younis mentions there is not much of a difference than the deck used in the last match. Adds that once the light comes on, it can get difficult to get runs. 250-260 should be a good score at this wicket.

New Zealand (Unchanged playing XI) - Devon Conway, Finn Allen, Kane Williamson (C), Daryl Mitchell, Tom Latham (WK), Glenn Phillips, Michael Bracewell, Mitchell Santner, Ish Sodhi, Tim Southee, Lockie Ferguson.

Pakistan (Playing XI) - Fakhar Zaman, Shan Masood (In for Imam-ul-Haq), Babar Azam (C), Mohammad Rizwan (WK), Haris Sohail, Agha Salman, Mohammad Nawaz, Mohammad Wasim, Usama Mir, Mohammad Hasnain (In for Naseem Shah), Haris Rauf.
TOSS - The coin goes up and lands in favour of Pakistan. They will BAT first.

The visitors will be pleased that senior players came to the party for New Zealand and helped them level the ODI series. The Kane Williamson-led unit will look to continue its good momentum and seal an away series on Asian soil. Pakistan though will make it difficult for visitors and avoid any undesirable results at home. Which side will come out on top? We shall find out together. Toss and team news in a bit.

The home side will really need to dig deep after another poor batting performance on the tour. Clearly, Pakistani batsmen failed to counter the consistent threat from New Zealand spinners in the previous match. Babar Azam has been the backbone of the batting order. Talking about the bowling, Pakistan has been quite commendable and collective with its approach. They will look to carry on with the same momentum.

Hello and a warm welcome at Karachi City Cricket Association Stadium, Karachi, Pakistan for the final game of the one-day series between Pakistan and New Zealand. Pakistan won the first one but the visitors bounced back and leveled the series 1-1, winning by a margin of 79 runs in the second. Both sides will be aiming for a series win and win this one. Let's see how this contest pans out. Stay tuned.
... MATCH DAY ...

It is time for the series decider of the New Zealand tour of Pakistan. Pakistan won the first game whilst Zealand bounced back in the second. New Zealand produced an impressive display with the bat and ball to level the three-match one-day series in Durban. With the series evenly poised at 1-1, Skipper Kane Williamson will be keen to make sure the side can put in a pitch-perfect performance in this game. On the other hand, Pakistan batted poorly and lost wickets at regular intervals to lose the second ODI by 79 runs. Babar Azam will be hoping that the batting lineup can learn from their mistakes and make significant improvements in the series decider. For the home side, in the batting department, the onus will be on the likes of Fakhar Zaman, Imam-ul-Haq, captain Babar Azam, wicket-keeper Mohammad Rizwan, and Haris Sohail to deliver the bulk of the runs. They will be looking to put up a gritty stand and win this one. In the first ODI, Mohammad Rizwan was the standout performer with the bat and finished the innings with the top score of 77 not out off 86 balls. He fumbled a bit in the second game. Their batting department was not up to the mark and they will be hoping to turn things around. On the flip side, the visitors will be relying on the likes of Finn Allen, Devon Conway, captain Kane Williamson, Glenn Phillips, Tom Latham, and Michael Bracewell to deliver the bulk of the runs. In the bowling department, the onus will be on the likes of Tim Southee, Henry Shipley, Mitchell Santner, Ish Sodhi, and Michael Bracewell to provide timely breakthroughs. Which team will come out on top? Let's find out together.
